The case of plaintiff, in short, is that, the suit land and other non suit land belonged to one Fazar Ali having 2/3 share and Khatunennese haying 1/3 share and accordingly CS khatian No. 310 was prepared in their names and thereafter by amicable partition, Fazar Ali got the suit land who died leaving behind two sons and one daughter and thereafter by amicable partition the suit land went to plaintiff Moti Miah and at the time of recent survey operation, plaintiff, being in physical possession, got the property recorded in his name in the BS khatian and thereafter took loan from Bangladesh Krishi Bank, Nasirnagar Branch, by mortgaging the suit land and was paying taxes and rent to the concerned authorities and the defendants did not possess the suit land and on several dates, they illegally dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land and hence the present suit. 

 4. The defendants appeared in the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and the case of the defendants is that the defendant No. 1 is the owner of the suit land by was of inheritance and purchase and accordingly, SA Khatian No. 310 was recorded in the name of defendant No. 1 in respect of the suit land and the plaintiff never possessed the suit land and defendant Nos. 2, 3 and 4, sons of defendant No. 1, on behalf of defendant No.1, were possessing the suit land and the suit is false and fabricated and is to be dismissed. 

 8. I have heard the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner and perused the revisional application along with other materials on record. It appears that the plaintiff, who is the present petitioner, filed a suit for recovery of possession under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act being Title Suit No. 16 of 2003 in the Court of Senior Assistant .Judge, Nasirnagar, Brahmanbaria impleading the opposite parties as defendants. The plaintiff claims that on the death of his father Fazar Ali, he by way of amicable partition, got the suit land and BS khatian was recorded in his name after which he took loan from Bangladesh Krishi Bank and was also paying rent and taxes regularly but thereafter he was dispossessed from the suit land by the defendants illegally. 

 10. All that a plaintiff in a suit under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act is required to prove is his possession and dispossession within six months next before the institution of the suit. Before a person call come under section 9 he has to show that he had actual physical possession of the immovable property from which he was dispossessed without his consent by the defendant within six months prior to the institution of the suit. Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act is concerned with physical possession and not with title. It appears that the plaintiffs witnesses, though could not mention the numbers of dag and khatian, categorically mentioned the date of possession and dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit land. The trial Court observed that most of the plaintiff witnesses could not remember the birth date of their children and their marriage dates along with date of the last Eid, for which their statements regarding the date of possession and dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit land can be tutored, which they memorised and deposed before the Court. The fact that the plaintiff witnesses did not remember the important dates of their lives and only one remembers the date of possession and dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit land brought doubt on the mind of the trial Court on the credibility of the deposition of plaintiff witnesses. In a suit for recovery of possession under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, notwithstanding any other title that may be set up in such a suit, the person dispossessed without the consent or otherwise than in due course of law, can claim for recovery of the possession.
